_comment: MOCK — sample data only, not real measurements. Internally consistent for interface testing. Used as contract for Phases 3, 4, 5.
cell_description: MOCK — South Shetland Islands, Antarctic basalt terrain (Deception Island area). Polar, basaltic, low albedo. This cell is a POOR illumination analog for Malapert Massif — intentional: illustrates that no Earth cell can match the lunar south-pole solar regime.

slope.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, resampled to 1 km

roughness.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 — std-dev of elevation in 3×3 km window

broadband_albedo.source: MODIS MCD43A3 broadband shortwave albedo, annual mean

lst_diurnal_range.source: MODIS MOD11A2 — mean of (day LST − night LST)

characteristic_scores.note: Percentile/regime comparison — absolute temperatures cannot be reproduced on Earth.

INTENTIONALLY LOW — this cell is a poor illumination analog for the lunar south pole. No Earth cell can match the Moon's obliquity-driven low-sun regime (max solar elevation ~1.5–6° all year). Earth minimum is ~23.4° (South Pole at summer solstice). Score discriminates correctly.

max_solar_elevation.source: Computed from latitude −62.875° (annual maximum solar elevation = 90 − |φ| + 23.44°)

mean_solar_elevation.earth_value_note: Computed by integrating solar elevation over 365 days weighted by day fraction above horizon
mean_solar_elevation.source: Computed from latitude −62.875° (annual mean solar elevation above horizon)

sun_fraction.earth_value_note: Computed: at -62.875°S no polar night (min noon elevation 3.68° > 0); fraction = 0.500 from sunrise/sunset integration
sun_fraction.source: Computed from latitude −62.875° (fraction of year sun > 0°; reference target Malapert has LOLA illumination fraction ~0.86)

environment_tag_rules.volcanic: GLiM vb class present (basaltic terrain, Deception Island area) → TRUE
environment_tag_rules.arid: aridity_score assumed 0.65 > 0.50 → TRUE (not in selected set; computed from stored scores)
environment_tag_rules.cave: volcanic_caves HIGH likelihood not confirmed → FALSE

cannot_reproduce: Solar elevation regime: lunar obliquity ~1.5° means the sun never rises above ~6° at the south pole all year. Earth's annual maximum solar elevation cannot drop below ~23.4° (South Pole at summer solstice). No Earth cell can replicate the near-horizon sun regime of the lunar south pole.
Gravity: 1/6 g (1.62 m/s²) — no terrestrial equivalent
Vacuum: ~10⁻¹⁰ Pa — no convection, no wind acoustics
Radiation: unfiltered solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays
Absolute temperatures: 40 K (PSR) to ~400 K (equatorial noon) — far outside any Earth surface range
14-day continuous daylight / 14-day darkness cycle — no terrestrial analog
Regolith: electrostatic, sharp-edged (no weathering) — no terrestrial surface-level equivalent
